01 — The Founder

About Jaylyn

Jaylyn

I started Motives Volume II because I kept noticing the same problem everywhere I looked. Either a brand was cheap and you could tell just by looking at it, or it was so expensive that nobody my age could actually get near it. I wanted to create something that felt genuinely premium but was built around a real vision and not just a price tag.

I have always been obsessed with the way clothes feel and look up close. Specifically the texture of a fabric and how it completely changes the energy of an outfit. That obsession is what this entire brand is built on.

My background with fashion started early. I have spent years paying attention to what separates a piece that just sits on a rack from one that actually stops people when you walk into a room. I study silhouettes, textures and the way certain materials move differently than others. That is the knowledge I bring into every piece we make at Motives Volume II and it is what makes me qualified to run this brand.

Entrepreneurial Inspiration — Jeff Bezos

Jeff Bezos started Amazon in 1994 out of his garage in Seattle with basically nothing. He was selling books online at a time when most people thought the internet was just a phase. He turned that into one of the biggest companies in history by staying obsessed with the customer and always thinking long term instead of chasing quick wins.

The thing that inspires me most about Bezos is his Day 1 mindset. He believed that the moment a company gets comfortable it starts dying. That is exactly how I want to run Motives Volume II. We treat every day like we are still building from scratch because in a lot of ways we always are.

02 — Business Structure

How We Are Organized

Selected Structure: Sole Proprietorship

A Sole Proprietorship is a business that is owned and run by one single person. There is no legal separation between the owner and the business. The owner keeps all the profits, makes every decision and takes on full personal responsibility for anything that happens with the business.

I chose this structure because Motives Volume II is entirely my vision. I am the creative director, the buyer, the strategist and the one making every call. As a brand just getting started I do not need partners making things complicated. I need full control and the ability to move fast. If the brand grows to a certain point I would look into switching to an LLC to protect my personal assets but right now a sole proprietorship fits perfectly.

03 — Compensation

How I Earn

As a sole proprietor I do not get a regular paycheck like an employee would. Instead I earn profit which is the money left over after I cover all of the business costs. So if I bring in 0,000 in sales and my fabric, packaging and marketing costs total ,000 then my profit is ,000 and that is my income. My earnings go up when the business does well and go down during slow months. That is the trade off and honestly it is the motivation too.

04 — Owner vs. Employee

Category Me (Self Employed) A Hired Employee
Total CompensationI earn profit after all business costs are covered. There is no cap on what I can make but it is also never guaranteed.Fixed salary or hourly wage paid on a consistent schedule like every two weeks or monthly.
Health InsuranceI pay for my own health insurance completely out of pocket since I have no employer covering any of it.The employer usually covers part or all of the health insurance premium as a benefit.
TaxesI handle all my own taxes including self employment tax on top of regular income tax and I file every quarter.The employer automatically takes taxes out of each paycheck so the employee does not have to think about it.
Work ScheduleI set my own hours but the reality is the business never really fully closes so I am always working in some way.A set schedule the employer defines. When the shift ends the employee is actually off.
Job SecurityMy income depends entirely on how well Motives Volume II performs. If sales slow down so does my pay.More stable overall since employees are protected by company HR policies and employment contracts.

The Blueprint

Business Plan

5 Year Vision

Year 1 — I plan to launch Motives Volume II completely online through Shopify. I will start with six debut pieces in limited quantities so the brand builds a reputation for being hard to get. My main customers will be fashion forward people between 18 and 32 and I will reach them through Instagram and TikTok.

Year 2 — I want to collaborate with one or two independent designers on a capsule collection and start reaching out to fashion publications to get the brand some real press coverage.

Year 3 — I plan to open a flagship showroom in either Dallas or Houston that works as both a retail space and a creative studio for shoots and brand events.

Years 4 and 5 — The goal is to expand internationally by landing a wholesale account in Paris or Tokyo and launching a made to order program for high end clients who want something fully custom.

Location and Operations

In the beginning everything will run online. I will store inventory at a small leased warehouse space in the Dallas Fort Worth area. The website will be my main storefront and I will drive traffic to it through consistent social media content and editorial photography that matches the brand aesthetic.

Business Resources

Support Network

Federal Level
Small Business Administration (SBA)

The SBA is a U.S. government agency that helps small businesses get started through loans, grants, mentorship and free counseling. For Motives Volume II the SBA could help me secure a startup loan to cover my first production run and connect me with a SCORE mentor who can walk me through the early stages of running the business.

State Level
Texas Economic Development and Tourism Office

This office provides grants, tax incentives and programs built specifically for small businesses operating in Texas. They run the Texas Small Business Credit Initiative which could help fund an early stage fashion brand like mine that is based in the state.

Local Level
Dallas Regional Chamber of Commerce

The Dallas Chamber connects local business owners with networking events, mentors and promotional opportunities. As a member Motives Volume II would get access to local press, pop up retail events and a real community of entrepreneurs dealing with the same challenges I am in the DFW area.

Risk Analysis

Risks & Rewards

Major Risks

  • I could lose my entire $17,000 investment if the brand does not generate enough sales in the first season to keep going.
  • The fashion industry is extremely competitive. Bigger brands already have the budgets and the customer loyalty that I am still working to build from scratch.
  • My income is unpredictable. A slow month means less money coming in and that makes it hard to plan things out financially on a personal level.

Major Rewards

  • I have full creative and financial ownership. Every profit dollar is mine and every decision about the brand is mine to make without asking anyone for permission.
  • I am building something with real long term value. A successful fashion brand is worth far more over time than any regular salary would ever be.
  • There is nothing like knowing that what you built came completely from your own vision and your own work. That feeling alone is a reward on top of everything else.

The Franchise Option

Why I Chose a Startup Over a Franchise

A franchise like Subway, a UPS Store or a fashion retail chain gives you a system that already works. The brand is already known and you are buying into something that has been tested. The risk is lower because someone else already figured out if the concept works. But franchise owners have to pay ongoing royalty fees that usually run between 5 and 10 percent of all their revenue. They also have to follow strict brand rules and have basically zero creative control. On top of that the upfront franchise fee can run anywhere from $30,000 to over $500,000 just to get started.

For Motives Volume II none of that made any sense. This brand exists because of a very specific vision around rare textures and editorial fashion that could never fit inside someone else's framework. The whole point is that it is original. Building something from scratch is definitely a bigger risk but the reward of owning something that is completely mine with its own identity and its own future is worth way more to me than any safety net a franchise could ever offer.
